 ORDER

The petitioners have filed the present petition under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 (herein after referred to as the Code) seeking quashment of order dated 06.10.2012 (Annexure P/6) passed on a private criminal complaint filed by respondent No.2, whereby Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Indore, District Indore (M.P.) has issued a bailable warrant for their presence on 12.12.2012.

entities.text: Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Indore, District Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Vide order dated 12.12.2012, notice was issued to the respondent No.2; and despite service of notice to respondent, he did not appear, hence, proceeded ex parte.
On 18.11.2013, this Court has stayed the further proceedings in Criminal Case No.36572 of 2012; and despite the aforesaid stay also, respondent No.2 is not appearing before this Court.
3. In short, the facts of the case are, as under: -

On 10.09.2008, the petitioners and respondent No.2 while working in Press Trust of India (PTI) collided with each other, which has resulted in lodging of First Information Report (FIR) against respondent No.2 at the instance of the petitioners at Crime No.995 of 2008 dated 10.09.2008 (Annexure P/2) at Police Station Palasia,
District Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 323, 294 and 506 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (herein after referred to as the IPC).
The Final Report was filed on 26.12.2008 (Annexure P/3) against respondent No.2.

On 17.02.2012 (Annexure P/4), the State of Madhya Pradesh decided to withdraw the aforesaid case in a Lok Adalat, for which the petitioners did not raise any objection and the matter was closed against respondent No.2.
4.

After closing of the aforesaid criminal case, respondent No.2 approached the Judicial Magistrate First Class, Indore, District Indore (M.P.) by way of written criminal complaint filed on 30.05.2012 Harshwardhan And 4 Ors. vs State Of M.P. And Anr. on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165261203/
2 (Annexure P/6) seeking cognizance against the present petitioners for commission of under Sections 294, 506, 120-B, 211, 324, 193, 420, 109, 198, 469 and 511 of the IPC.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 (B.R. Bhaskar) examined himself as Witness No.1, Dharmendra Shukla as Witness No.2, Mohan Yadav as Witness No.3 and Surendra Prasad as Witness No.4.

5 . After registration of the complaint, Learned Magistrate before taking cognizance on proposed charges, heard the complainant's counsel and vide order dated 06.10.2012 (Annexure P/6) decided to take cognizance under Section 323 read with Section 34 of the IPC against the petitioners and issued bailable warrant.
Hence, this petition before this Court.

6. Shri Ajay Bagadiya, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the learned Magistrate has categorically recorded a finding that this complaint is filed on 30.05.2012 of an alleged incident which took place on 10.09.2008 and apparently, same is time barred, but wrongly held that once the Court has taken cognizance, now the complaint cannot be closed.

Learned Court has wrongly opined that the Court has taken cognizance under Section 200 of the Code upon filing of the complaint on 30.05.2012, whereas the cognizance was taken only on 06.10.2012, which is beyond the period of one year, as provided under Section 468 (2) of the Code, hence petitioners are liable to be discharged.

7. Shri Sudarshan Joshi, learned Government Advocate appearing for respondent No.1 - State of Madhya Pradesh submits that from the language of Section 200 of the Code, it is apparent that the Magistrate takes the cognizance upon filing of a complaint, therefore, once the cognizance has been taken, the Court cannot review its own order by discharging the accused persons.
Heard.
8. Vide impugned order dated 06.10.2012, the learned Court has held that the offence took taken place on "10.09.2008" and the private criminal complaint is filed on "30.05.2012".

Section 468 (2)
of the Code puts a bar for taking cognizance, after expiry of period of one year, if the offence is punishable with imprisonment or fine not acceding one year.

For the alleged offence under Section 323 of the IPC, the maximum punishment is one year, therefore, from the date "10.09.2008", when the offence was said to have been committed, the complaint in writing is filed on "30.05.2012"
which is admittedly beyond the period of limitation.
9.

So far as contention of Shri Sudarshan Joshi, learned Government Advocate, that the date of filing of the complaint is the date when learned Magistrate takes cognizance on a private criminal complaint, is not correct, because Section 200 of the Code says that after filing of a complaint in writing, the Magistrate calls upon the complainant to examine himself on oath and the witnesses, if any.

Thereafter, under Section 201 of the Code, upon a complaint, if the Magistrate finds himself not competent to take cognizance, he shall, either return the complaint to the complainant for presentation before the proper Court, or if the complaint is not in writing, direct the complainant to the proper Court.

Thereafter, under Section 202 of the Code, the Magistrate, who is authorized to take cognizance or which has been made over to him under Section 192 of the Code, if he thinks fit,
he shall in case where the accused is residing at place or beyond the area, either himself can inquire,
Harshwardhan And 4 Ors. vs State Of M.P. And Anr. on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165261203/
3 or direct the Police to investigate into the matter.

entities.text: Harshwardhan And 4 Ors. vs State Of M.P. And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Likewise, under Section 204 of the Code, if in the opinion of the Magistrate taking cognizance of an offence there is sufficient ground for proceeding in the case appears to be, in a summon-case, issue summons for attendance of the accused; in a warrant-case, he may issue a warrant, if he thinks fit.
Therefore, this would be a stage on which, the learned Magistrate takes the cognizance on any complaint i.e. the date on which an order under Section 204 of the Code is passed.

10. In the present case also, the complaint sought prosecution of the present petitioners under various sections of IPC, but the learned Magistrate, after examining the averments in the complaint and the statement of the witnesses found that the present petitioners / accused are liable to be prosecuted only under Section 323/34 of IPC, therefore, the Magistrate has taken cognizance only under this section and not in other sections of IPC.

Therefore, Shri Ajay Bajagiya, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners is right in making submission that the learned Court has taken cognizance only on "06.10.2012"
against the petitioners, which is beyond the period of one year from the date of the incident i.e. "10.09.2008".

11. Hence, in this view of the matter, impugned order dated 06.10.2012 (Annexure P/6) passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Indore, District Indore (M.P.) on a private criminal complaint filed by respondent No.2 as well as further proceeding in Criminal Case No.36572 of 2012 pending before the trial Court are hereby quashed.
